events.text: {npc} cuts your kite string with a sharpened one of {his} own and your kite sails off over the river. The whole street saw.

mem.note: fetched the kite out of the river and waved it at me

ok.log: You come back soaked with the kite over your head. The street cheers. {npc} goes home early.

fail.log: The river takes the kite and nearly takes you. {npc} pulls you out by the collar, then tells everyone.

mem.note: cut my kite string back

effects.log: Two kites in the river. Two mothers on the doorstep. A war is declared that will last forty years.

events.text: The village teacher praises {npc}'s calligraphy and holds yours up as the example of what not to do. {npc} smiles at you across the room.

choices.text: Practise every night until yours is better

mem.note: practised till their hand was better than mine

effects.log: By spring the teacher holds up both. {npc} stops smiling across the room.

mem.note: spilled ink on my best page

effects.log: Satisfying for a day. The teacher makes you copy the whole classic twice.

variants: The village teacher holds up {npc}'s calligraphy as a model and yours as a warning. Across the room, {npc} smiles at you.

events.text: A stray dog follows you home and {npc} swears it is {his}. The dog, sitting between you, refuses to have an opinion.

mem.note: won the dog from me

ok.log: The dog walks to you and lies on your feet. {npc} does not speak to you, or the dog, for a month.

mem.note: watched the dog choose me

fail.log: The dog goes to {npc}. {He} is unbearable about it for a year.

mem.note: gave me the dog without a fight

effects.log: {npc} is suspicious for a week, then names the dog after you, which may or may not be a compliment.

variants: A stray dog trots home behind you, and {npc} insists it is {his}. The dog sits down between you and declines to take sides.

events.text: {npc} dares you to climb down the old well where the village says a drowned scholar lives. {He} will hold the rope.

mem.note: came up from the well with a prize

ok.log: No scholar. A clump of glowing herb on a ledge. You climb up with it in your teeth.

fail.log: {npc} lets the rope slip, just a little, just for a laugh. You climb out with a twisted ankle and a long memory.

mem.note: held the rope steady

effects.log: {npc} climbs down, shrieks, climbs up. You never let the rope slip. {He} never mentions it, which is how you know.

variants: {npc} bets you will not go down the old well where the drowned scholar is said to live. {He} offers to hold the rope.

events.text: A sect's recruiter comes through town and will take one child. {npc} and you are the last two standing in the yard.

mem.note: took the recruiter's place from me

ok.log: The recruiter points at you. {npc} watches you climb onto the cart and does not wave.

mem.note: lost the recruiter's bout to me

fail.log: The recruiter points at {npc}. {He} waves from the cart, which is worse.

mem.note: stepped back so I could go

effects.log: {npc} goes with the recruiter and writes you one letter in five years, which says only: I have not forgotten.

variants: A recruiter from a sect passes through and says there is room for one child. By sunset only you and {npc} are still standing in the dusty yard.
The sect's recruiter has tested every child in town and wants exactly one. It comes down, as everyone knew it would, to you and {npc}.

events.text: {npc} tells half the town a secret you told only {him}, years ago, when you were friends for one summer.

mem.note: told the town my secret back

effects.log: The town enjoys a week of both of you. Neither of you enjoys it at all.

choices.text: Say nothing and let it pass

mem.note: never paid me back for the secret

effects.log: It passes. {npc} is ashamed, quietly, for longer than you are.

events.text: You and {npc} find the same torn manual page in the market's waste bin and grab it at the same moment.

mem.note: tore the page in half with me

effects.log: Each of you learns half a technique. Neither of you ever quite forgets which half.

mem.note: studied the page with me

effects.log: One afternoon on the riverbank, heads together. You both pretend afterwards that it never happened.

variants: In the rubbish behind the market you spot a torn page of a martial manual. So does {npc}. Your hands close on it at the same instant.

events.text: In a tavern, {npc} and three of {his} new sect brothers are about to beat a drunk who spilled wine on them. The drunk is old and very drunk.

mem.note: stopped me in front of my brothers

ok.log: The old man walks out on two feet. {npc} remembers who stood in the way.

mem.note: took a beating for a drunk

fail.log: You take the beating meant for the drunk, and the old man walks out on two feet. {npc} remembers who stood in the way.

choices.text: Buy the old man a cup and seat the drunk

mem.note: made the fight go away with a cup of wine

effects.log: The moment passes. {npc}'s brothers laugh. {npc} does not.

variants: {npc} and three of {his} new sect brothers have an old drunk backed against the tavern wall over a spilled cup of wine. The old man can barely stand.

events.text: A matchmaker proposes, to both your families, the same person for both of you. The town treats it as a horse race.

mem.note: withdrew from the match

effects.log: {npc} wins a race with no other runner and looks oddly cheated by it.

mem.note: won the match my family wanted

ok.log: The town settles its bets in your favour. Nobody asked the person being matched, who marries a third party within the year.

mem.note: lost the match to me

fail.log: The town settles its bets, and you lose them. Nobody asked the person being matched, who marries a third party within the year.

variants: A matchmaker has proposed the same person to both your family and the family of your old rival. The whole town is laying bets.

events.text: You both apply for the same post: a guard's place at the county magistrate's. There is one place and two of you, and the captain wants a bout.

mem.note: took the guard post from me

ok.log: You get the uniform. {npc} gets a story to tell about the one who did.

mem.note: lost the guard post to me

fail.log: {npc} gets the uniform. You get a story to tell about the one who did.

choices.text: Let {him} have it and take the night watch elsewhere

mem.note: let me have the post

effects.log: {npc} takes the post and is good at it. Years later {he} looks the other way for you once, without being asked.

variants: There is one guard's post open at the county magistrate's, and both of you want it. The captain settles it the simple way: a bout.

events.text: A letter arrives from {npc}, who is now somewhere far: a long account of {his} victories, with one line at the end asking how you are, as if by accident.

choices.text: Write back with your own victories

mem.note: wrote back bragging

effects.log: The letters go on for years, each one longer. Neither of you ever writes the line at the end first.

choices.text: Write back only the answer to the last line

mem.note: answered only the last line

effects.log: {npc} does not write again for a year. Then a short letter, with no victories in it at all.

variants: A courier brings a thick letter from {npc}, who is far away now: page after page of duels won and honours taken, and squeezed into the margin at the very end, "And you? Are you well?"
{npc} writes from the other end of the empire. The letter is mostly about how well {he} is doing. The last line, in smaller characters, asks after your health.

events.text: Two sects are at war over a border town, and {npc} commands one side's patrol. You meet in the empty market at dawn, alone.

choices.text: Settle the town between the two of you

mem.note: won the town from me alone in the market

ok.log: Two sects, one duel, no war. The elders on both sides are furious that it worked.

mem.note: lost the market duel

fail.log: You lose the duel, but {npc} keeps the bargain and calls off the patrol. Two sects, one duel, no war, and the wrong winner.

choices.text: Talk about the war ending instead

mem.note: talked about peace in the empty market

ok.log: The war ends a season early. Nobody on either side knows who to thank, which suits you both.

mem.note: talked when we should have fought

fail.log: Your words do not carry. The war runs its season, and you and {npc} part with nothing settled.

variants: Two sects are fighting over a border town, and {npc} leads one side's patrol. At dawn you meet in the deserted market square, the two of you and nobody else.
The war between the sects has emptied the border town. At first light you walk into the silent market and find {npc}, captain of the other patrol, waiting alone.

events.text: A demonic cultivator has been taking disciples from every sect in the province. {npc} comes to your door at night with a map and a very small smile.

mem.note: hunted the demon with me

ok.log: Back to back in the dark, and the demon falls. Afterwards neither of you can remember who was the rival and who was the friend.

mem.note: bled beside me in the lair

fail.log: The lair is deeper than the map said. {npc} drags you out of it, and afterwards neither of you can remember who was the rival and who was the friend.

choices.text: Hunt alone. You do not need {him}

mem.note: hunted the demon alone

ok.log: You get the credit. {npc} gets there five minutes late, with the map.

mem.note: needed rescuing in the end

fail.log: The lair is worse than you thought. {npc} gets there five minutes late, with the map, and carries you out.

variants: Disciples are vanishing from sects all over the province, and every trail ends at the same demonic cultivator. Tonight {npc} knocks on your door with a hand-drawn map and the smallest of smiles.
A demonic cultivator has been stealing disciples from every hall in the province. {npc} turns up at your gate after dark, unrolls a map on your table, and waits for you to say it first.

events.text: {npc}'s child turns up at your gate asking to be your disciple, because, the child says, {npc} talks about nobody else.

choices.text: Take the child as a disciple

mem.note: took my child as a disciple

effects.log: {npc} is furious, then proud, then furious again. The child is gifted and very like both of you.

choices.text: Send the child home with a letter

mem.note: sent my child back with a letter

effects.log: The letter says: teach your own child. {npc} keeps it on the wall.

events.text: {npc} sends an invitation written in a hand that shakes: tea, at the old pine on the hill, one afternoon, nothing else.

mem.note: came to the old pine for tea

effects.log: You sit under the pine you raced up a lifetime ago. You argue about who won. Neither of you remembers. It is a good afternoon.

choices.text: Send a better tea, and stay home

mem.note: sent tea instead of coming

effects.log: {npc} drinks it alone under the pine and tells the children it is from the only person {he} ever lost to.

events.text: A rumour says {npc} is dying. {His} disciples ask whether you will speak at the funeral, when it comes, since {he} asked for you by name.

choices.text: Agree, and visit while {he} can still hear

mem.note: came while I could still hear it

effects.log: {He} recovers, out of spite, {he} says, so that you will have to wait. You both laugh for the first time in decades.

choices.text: Agree, and write the words now

effects.log: You write all night. The words are kinder than anything you ever said to {his} face, and you put them in a drawer.
